advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Handle the SC-before-AC ordering in rewrite_description's merge path (currently produces a reversed/empty slice and leaves the SC block in place).
evidence: `description[: ac["heading_end"]] + merged_ac_body + description[ac["end"] : sc["start"]] + description[sc["end"] :]`

All merge test inputs order AC first: tests/scripts/test_migrate_success_criteria_heldout.py:67 `"## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] here

## Success Criteria
- there
"`
ABSENCE: no test exercises a description where `## Success Criteria` appears before `## Acceptance Criteria`.
`items = [ln.strip() for ln in sc_checkbox_body.split("\n") if ln.strip().startswith("- [")]`
Rename path preserves full body: line 75 `... + _AC_HEADING + sc_checkbox_body + ...`

ABSENCE: prose-preservation (test_non_bullet_prose_inside_the_block_is_not_checkboxed) and subheading tests (test_a_subheading_does_not_terminate_the_block) only exercise the rename path (no AC block present).
advisory.finding: The merge path assumes the AC block appears before the SC block in the description. When `## Success Criteria` precedes `## Acceptance Criteria`, `sc["start"] < ac["end"]`, so `description[ac["end"] : sc["start"]]` is an empty reversed slice and the SC section is never removed; the SC heading/body is instead retained inside `description[:ac["heading_end"]]` and content is duplicated/dropped.
merged_from: In the merge path, only lines starting with `- [` are collected into the AC block; any non-bullet prose or `###` subheadings inside the SC block are silently discarded. The rename-in-place path preserves them, so behavior is asymmetric and the merge path loses content.
scenarios: A ticket whose description places Success Criteria above Acceptance Criteria.
advisory.suggested_fix: Reconstruct the description by operating on the two section spans order-independently (e.g. remove the SC span first, then re-locate and append into AC), rather than assuming ac['end'] <= sc['start'].

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Match `## Success Criteria` / `## Acceptance Criteria` headings case-insensitively (mirroring `_count_ac_items`) so variant-case blocks are migrated.
evidence: scripts/migrate_success_criteria.py:24-25: `_SC_HEADING = "## Success Criteria"` / `_AC_HEADING = "## Acceptance Criteria"`
scripts/migrate_success_criteria.py:64: `sc = next((s for s in sections if s["heading"] == _SC_HEADING), None)` — exact-string equality on the stripped heading line

src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py:159: `if ln.lower().startswith("## acceptance criteria"):` — the floor matches case-INSENSITIVELY, so the migration's case-sensitive scan under-selects rows the floor cares about
scripts/migrate_success_criteria.py:70: `ac = next((s for s in sections if s["heading"] == _AC_HEADING), None)` — exact match; a heading like `## Acceptance Criteria (v2)` yields `ac is None`
scripts/migrate_success_criteria.py:72-76: `if ac is None:` branch renames SC to `_AC_HEADING` in place, leaving the pre-existing variant AC heading untouched → duplicate AC sections
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py:159-164: the floor resets counting at the next `## ` heading, so a second AC heading changes which items are counted
advisory.finding: The migration matches the `## Success Criteria` / `## Acceptance Criteria` headings by EXACT string equality, but the check-ac floor it targets counts the AC heading CASE-INSENSITIVELY, so tickets whose criteria live under a variant-case heading (e.g. `## Success criteria`, `## SUCCESS CRITERIA`) are never migrated and remain invisible to the blocking floor — an incomplete backfill.
merged_from: Because the AC-block lookup uses exact heading equality, a ticket whose acceptance section carries any trailing text on the heading line (e.g. `## Acceptance Criteria (draft)`) is NOT recognized as an existing AC block, so the migration takes the `ac is None` branch and renames the SC section to `## Acceptance Criteria` in place — producing TWO acceptance-criteria headings in one description.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide and document whether archived tickets are in scope; if so, pass `include_archived=True` (with `exclude_deleted=True`) to `list_tickets` so archived closed tickets are covered.
evidence: scripts/migrate_success_criteria.py:100: `tickets = rebar.list_tickets(repo_root=repo_root, full=True)` — no `include_archived` passed
src/rebar/_lib_reads.py:112: `include_archived: bool = False,` — archived tickets are dropped by default
src/rebar/_lib_reads.py:123-125: docstring notes delete writes STATUS(deleted)+ARCHIVED so archived-exclusion also hides tombstones — but legitimately-archived closed tickets are hidden too
advisory.finding: `propose_migrations` scans via `rebar.list_tickets(..., full=True)` without `include_archived=True`, and `list_tickets` defaults `include_archived=False`; closed tickets that have been archived are therefore excluded from the backfill even though they may carry unmigrated `## Success Criteria` blocks.
